title: Maize stem borer colonization, establishment and crop damage levels in a maize-leucaena agroforestry system in Kenya
exp_design: Plots were laid out in randomized complete block design, with five replications at Mtwapa and four at Amoyo.
time_raw: The study covered six cropping seasons from October 1992 to August 1995 long rains: April–June, short rains: mid-October–mid-December
T_subpractice_description_raw: Intercrop 1.5 m: maize were planted between leucaena hedgerows planted 1.5 m apart
T_intercrop_subpractice_raw: Intercrop 1.5 m: maize were planted between leucaena hedgerows planted 1.5 m apart
T_weed_method_raw: Intercrop 1.5 m: maize were planted between leucaena hedgerows planted 1.5 m apart
T_residues_subpractice_raw: Intercrop 1.5 m: maize were planted between leucaena hedgerows planted 1.5 m apart. Plots were mulch with leucaena leaves. During maize planting (at the onset of rains), trees were cut back to 30 cm above ground. Plots were mulched with leucaena leaves, except for one of the 2.25 m plots, and regularly weeded, except for another of the 2.25 m plots.
C_out_exp_design: Randomised block design with five replicates, where the study covered 6 cropping seasons (so yield N = 6 x 5). Three species of stem-borers were encountered at Mtwapa; Sesamia calamistis, C. partel- lus and Chilo orichalcociliellus. Dispensers were loaded with the synthetic pheromone between 1400 and 1500 hours and mounted on sticky Phercon I C traps which were placed 50 cm above the ground, one at the center of each plot between 1600 and 1800 hours the same day (Lux et al., 1994). Adult moths were collected and counted twice weekly (Wednesday and Sunday) for a period of one year (December 1993 to November 1994). Fresh pheromone was loaded onto the traps during each moth collection day. Data about the total number of male moths were analysed. Abundance per plot (5 plots per treatment)

title: Maize stem borer colonization, establishment and crop damage levels in a maize-leucaena agroforestry system in Kenya
exp_design: Plots were laid out in randomized complete block design, with five replications at Mtwapa and four at Amoyo.
time_raw: The study covered six cropping seasons from October 1992 to August 1995 long rains: April–June, short rains: mid-October–mid-December
T_subpractice_description_raw: Intercrop 1.5 m: maize were planted between leucaena hedgerows planted 1.5 m apart

During maize planting (at the onset of rains), trees were cut back to 30 cm above ground. Plots were mulched with leucaena leaves, except for one of the 2.25 m plots, and regularly weeded, except for another of the 2.25 m plots.
C_out_exp_design: Randomised block design with five replicates, where the study covered 6 cropping seasons (so yield N = 6 x 5). Three species of stem-borers were encountered at Mtwapa; Sesamia calamistis, C. partel- lus and Chilo orichalcociliellus. Dispensers were loaded with the synthetic pheromone between 1400 and 1500 hours and mounted on sticky Phercon I C traps which were placed 50 cm above the ground, one at the center of each plot between 1600 and 1800 hours the same day (Lux et al., 1994). Adult moths were collected and counted twice weekly (Wednesday and Sunday) for a period of one year (December 1993 to November 1994). Fresh pheromone was loaded onto the traps during each moth collection day. Data about the total number of male moths were analysed. Abundance per plot (5 plots per treatment)
